units.text: Amazon F S X is a family of managed file systems. Use it when your workload needs a particular file protocol or file-system feature, rather than simply a place to store objects. For a Windows team share, F S X for Windows File Server fits S M B, Active Directory, and Windows file permissions. For a simulation reading large datasets in parallel, choose Lustre for high-throughput file access.

When you need NetApp data-management features and clients using N F S, S M B, or eye scuzzy, compare F S X for NetApp On Tap. For an N F S workload that relies on Z F S snapshots and clones, consider F S X for Open Z F S. ay double-you ess manages the file-system infrastructure. You still choose the family that fits the application's protocol, performance, and recovery needs.

ay double-you ess Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to ay double-you ess storage while keeping the interface those applications already use. Pick a gateway by what the local application expects. With S three File Gateway, a client uses N F S or S M B and its files become objects in S three. A block server uses eye scuzzy instead, so choose Volume Gateway. Cached volumes keep the main data in ay double-you ess with a local cache.

Stored volumes keep the main data on premises and back it up to ay double-you ess as snapshots. If your backup software expects a tape library, Tape Gateway presents virtual tapes over eye scuzzy. The existing backup workflow can send tapes to an ay double-you ess archive. Start with the client interface: file share, block disk, or tape library.
